title: The Ordinary Interior
premise: Astrid Eastwick has spent twenty years measuring bridges and avoiding the cracks in her own life: a dutiful marriage to a kind but distant husband, an unspoken estrangement from her sister, and a childhood home she swore never to revisit. When that home — where her mother's memory is dissolving into auction lots and strangers' bids — goes up for sale, Astrid returns to catalog what remains. Sorting through her mother's belongings with her sister Wren and an unexpected found family of neighbors and auction workers, she uncovers letters revealing her mother's own impossible choice between love and duty. As the auction day approaches, Astrid must decide whether truth or loyalty will define the rest of her life; she chooses truth, sells the house to the neighbors who loved her mother best, and finally speaks the unsaid — to her sister, and then, tentatively, to herself.
about_author: M. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former structural engineer who spent a decade inspecting coastal bridges before turning to fiction full-time. Their work examines the quiet load-bearing structures of family life, and they write from a small house within sight of a suspension span.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On a bridge inspection, she measures tolerances with practiced precision while mentally measuring her marriage — ten years of small silences with her husband Theo. The emotional beat is quiet unease: everything technically sound, nothing truly connected.

chapters.title: The Notice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A certified letter arrives: her childhood home on Kestrel Lane enters probate auction following her mother's death two years prior. She hasn't opened her mother's boxes since the funeral. Beat: dread disguised as administrative calm.

chapters.title: What Theo Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She tells Theo she'll be gone three weeks for the estate. He offers to come; she deflects with logistics. A tender, failed conversation at dinner shows how fluently they both avoid each other. Beat: loneliness inside companionship.

chapters.title: Kestrel Lane
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She arrives at the shuttered house and finds Wren already there, hostile and grieving in equal measure. Their first exchange reopens the old wound — Wren stayed through their mother's decline; Astrid did not. Beat: cold recognition.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Astrid catalogs the house room by room like an inspection report; interspersed flashbacks show young Astrid leaving at eighteen after a fight she's never fully remembered honestly. Beat: guilt surfacing through objects.

chapters.title: The Auctioneer's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dev, a warm, unhurried apprentice auctioneer, arrives to appraise the contents and treats each object as a story rather than a lot. His ease disarms Astrid. Beat: first breath of unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn Wren's side: years of caregiving, resentment banked like interest, and her own secret — she's been offered a job abroad she can't take without admitting she's exhausted. Beat: sympathy shifts toward Wren.

chapters.title: The Blue Room
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the locked blue room, Astrid finds a shoebox of letters addressed to someone named 'C.' — her mother's handwriting, intimate and unguarded. She pockets one, ashamed. Beat: the past becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Neighbors at the Fence
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Astrid's POV. Marisol and Ted Okonkwo, lifelong neighbors, bring food and memories, revealing their mother's last years were warmer than Astrid knew. Astrid realizes strangers witnessed her mother's tenderness. Beat: grief complicated by gratitude.

chapters.title: Load Rating
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, via phone calls and a brief visit. Theo arrives unannounced, sees Astrid laughing with Dev over a broken piano, and quietly registers the distance between them. He says nothing. Beat: the marriage measured and found wanting.

chapters.title: Letter to C.
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reading the letter fully, Astrid learns her mother once loved someone she gave up — choosing duty, the house, the girls. The parallel to Astrid's own careful, loveless caution lands hard. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren discovers the missing letter and accuses Astrid of stealing even now, even this. The fight detonates twenty years of silence about why Astrid really left at eighteen. Beat: rupture — the worst thing said aloud.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. After the fight, a storm knocks power out; the sisters shelter together and, in the dark, fragments of truth emerge — Astrid left because she saw something in the blue room as a teenager she never understood until now. Beat: first crack of reconciliation.

chapters.title: Dev's Offer
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, whose found-family philosophy was forged in foster care, gently challenges Astrid: loyalty to a memory isn't the same as loyalty to the living. He asks her, plainly, what she wants. Beat: invitation to honesty.

chapters.title: The Probate File
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Digging into paperwork, Astrid discovers their mother refinanced the house years ago to pay Wren's father's debts — a sacrifice Wren never knew. The ledger of who owed whom tilts entirely. Beat: loyalty recontextualized.

chapters.title: What Astrid Saw
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Astrid's POV. Sixteen-year-old Astrid walked into the blue room and saw her mother with C. — a moment of tenderness she reported, inadvertently, causing the ending of the affair and her mother's retreat into duty. Beat: the origin wound revealed.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid tells Wren everything: what she saw, what she caused, why she fled. Wren's fury breaks into grief, then something like relief — the mystery of their mother explained at last. Beat: catharsis through truth.

chapters.title: Bidding War
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Auction day. A developer outbids everyone; the Okonkwos stretch desperately; Wren, without telling Astrid, uses her relocation money to counter-bid. Tension peaks as the gavel hovers. Beat: climax — everything wagered.

chapters.title: The Gavel Falls
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid stops the bidding by publicly telling the room the house's true story — her mother, C., the sacrifices — and persuades the developer to withdraw, letting the Okonkwos win at a fair price. Truth, spoken aloud, saves the house. Beat: climax resolved through honesty.

chapters.title: Speaking the Unsaid
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid calls Theo and tells him the marriage has failed not from cruelty but from silence; they agree to separate with kindness. It hurts and frees her. Beat: the second truth, costlier and cleaner.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Wren and Astrid's shared POV. The sisters clean the house one final time, leave the blue-room letters with the Okonkwos, and Wren accepts the job abroad — knowing Astrid will visit. Beat: found family formalized, blood family repaired.

chapters.title: The Ordinary Interior
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. Months later, Astrid inspects a new bridge, then drives past Kestrel Lane where lights burn warm in windows. She keeps her inventory habit — but now writes down things worth saying, too. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
